new_statements.quote: KLEMTOON. Op enkele uitzonderingen na, hebben alle woorden den klemtoon op de voorlaatste lettergreep, hetzij dit een stamwoord of een afgeleid woord is. Voorvoegsels veranderen den klemtoon niet, alleen bij het achtervoegsel noka (imperf) krijgt dit den klemtoon. VOORBEELDEN. matatóeoe, mensch; belelíain, aangezicht; sosóloei, ring; poporáa, lattenspel; ngkíing, helft, andere kant; fóeloein, huidhaar; takólo, rug; tagalígoe, nagel; hása, slijpen; pangahása, slijpsteen; mése', koken; kamése', doen koken; mangkamése', gaan koken ... Met suffix: tóeoi, zitten; toeoinóka, zat; hána', klimmen; hanangnóka, klom; káin, eten; kainóka, at.
new_statements.translation: STRESS. With a few exceptions, all words have the stress on the penultimate syllable, whether the word is a root or a derived word. Prefixes do not change the stress; only with the suffix -noka (imperfective) does this [suffix] receive the stress. EXAMPLES: matatóeoe 'person'; belelíain 'face'; sosóloei 'ring'; ... hása 'whet', pangahása 'whetstone'; mése' 'cook', kamése' 'make cook', mangkamése' 'go and cook' ... With suffix: tóeoi 'sit', toeoinóka 'sat'; hána' 'climb', hanangnóka 'climbed'; káin 'eat', kainóka 'ate'. (p.2, on vowels: 'Since the accentuation of these words falls on the penultimate syllable...')
new_statements.citation: Fortgens, J. 1921. Bijdrage tot de kennis van het Sobojo (eiland Taliabo, Soela-groep). 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff (uitgegeven door het Koninklijk Instituut voor de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde van Ned.-Indie). new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened the page image (printed p.10, header 'BIJDRAGE TOT DE KENNIS VAN HET SOBOJO') and the Delpher scanned (scan page 00014). The KLEMTOON paragraph is there word for word: 'Op enkele uitzonderingen na, hebben alle woorden den klemtoon op de voorlaatste lettergreep, hetzij dit een stamwoord of een afgeleid woord is. Voorvoegsels veranderen den klemtoon niet, alleen bij het achtervoegsel noka (imperf) krijgt dit den klemtoon.' followed by VOORBEELDEN matatóeoe, belelíain, sosóloei(c), poporáa, ngkíing, fóeloein, takólo, tagalígoe, hása, pangahása, mése', kamése', mangkamése', déle, kadéle, mangkadéle and 'Met suffix: tóeoi(c), zitten; toeoinóka, zat; hána', klimmen; hanangnóka, klom…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the word, in roots and derived words alike; prefixation leaves it in place (stress stays on the root penult = word penult since prefixes precede), and the disyllabic imperfective suffix -noka carries the stress on its first syllable (kainóka), i.e. stress is recomputed on the suffixed word and remains penultimate. Final orthographic -in (weak final n) and final rising diphthongs count as belonging to the last syllable (fóeloein, tóeoi, sosóloei). Stated for Sobojo; Kadai differs segmentally (no final consonants, tala for talain) with no stress difference reported.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Op enkele uitzonderingen na' (a few exceptions) not enumerated in the rule; the sketch marks stress with an acute where cited, and at least one final-stressed form appears on the same page (sesóng 'zweet' [sweat], p.10); the Holle 'Taliabu' list convention (Stokhof 1980:3) likewise underlines accent only when not penultimate.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule ('alle woorden.. stamwoord of afgeleid woord'), illustrated with citation forms and affixed verbs; Fortgens adds (p.2) that Sobojo speak very fast and that open/close vowel allophones depend on the stressed syllable. Applies first-hand to Sobojo (W Taliabu, tali1262); extension to Kadai (kada1286) is by dialectal proximity only.
new_statements.identity_note: The only first-hand stress statement found (Fortgens 1921:10, and p.2) describes SOBOJO/Soboyo, the West-Taliabu variety filed in Glottolog under Taliabu tali1262, not Kadai (kada1286, East/South Taliabu + W Mangole). Fortgens collected 'Sobojo en Kadai' on the same trips and his sketch notes Kadai only as differing by loss of all final consonants and of final -in (p.2, p.8: 'welke laatste uitspraak dan ook die der Kadai is'); he gives no separate Kadai stress remark, and his Kadai Holle list (Stokhof 1980, list 150/166, pp.23-38) carries no accent note, whereas the companion 'Taliabu (Mohammedanen van Likitobi)' list 149/161 (p.3) has the note 'underlining indicates the accent when it is not placed on the penultimate syllable'. Collins 1989 (per Bloyd 2020:§ lit. review) and Ridwan et al. 2020 treat Kadai, Siboyo and Mange as dialects of one Taliabu language, so the Sobojo rule is the nearest proxy, but attributing it to kada1286 is an inference; the Fortgens material saved here should be cross-filed to tali1262.

sources.note: p.10 'Klemtoon': with few exceptions all words (root or derived) have stress on the penultimate syllable; prefixes do not shift stress; the imperfective suffix -noka takes the stress (tóeoi ~ toeoinóka, hána' ~ hanangnóka, káin ~ kainóka). p.2: vowel quality of a/e/o depends on stress; 'de accentueering dezer woorden valt op de voorlaatste lettergreep'. Object language is Sobojo; Kadai mentioned only for loss of final consonants (p.2) and of final -in (p.8); no Kadai-specific stress remark.

sources.note: p.22, second-hand from Fortgens: 'Fortgens maintains (2-3) that the Soboyo vowels have open and close allophones that are dependent on the placement of stress (penultimate in the word).. Stress placement (10) shows that these [final diphthongs] are phonological units: [mése?] 'cook', [matatúu] 'person', [túoi] 'sit', [sosólui] 'ring'.' Notes Fortgens gives 'comparative observations on its close relative, Kadai (eastern Taliabu)'.
